summary:
Firstly, our project focuses on a problem. Over the last 20 years, the number of astronauts has decreased by 73%. This could lead to other problems, such as a lack of experience and expertise in this field.

Our solution is to make children more aware of astronomy and space through a game called Marvive, which develops their curiosity and provides them with useful information that can improve their astronomy vocabulary. In short, our game is both educational and fun for 7–12-year-olds.

You might ask what makes Marvive so special. On the website, you can choose between two different platforms to play on: one is Unity, and the other is an HTML5 engine. In the Unity version, all the designs are created by us, which means they are unique. On both platforms, the only difference is the gameplay; the story is the same and is, again, our own creation.

We believe that Marvive has a bright future in different industries and could be developed easily. If we add new levels and strategies, Marvive could become a prominent game in the gaming industry.

Besides, how do we believe this solution is going to work? In the literature, there is some research on the effects of playing games on future career plans, and the main idea is that games can influence children's occupational ideas. We believe that the earlier, the better. If we start encouraging children early, we will solve the problem sustainably.

Thank you for reading.
details:
About the Project

Our game is a browser-based experience that runs entirely on our own website, with no downloads or installations required. It is currently available in two distinct versions, each offering a different way to play.

The first version is a Unity-built WebGL release, bringing rich interactivity and a polished feel directly to the browser. The second version runs on the website’s own code, written with JavaScript, CSS, and HTML5. Because it relies on standard web technologies, it stays lightweight, fast, and accessible on a wide range of devices.

The two versions also differ in style and spirit. One is a visual novel-style adventure, driven by story, characters, and meaningful choices. The other is an open-world exploration game, inviting players to wander freely, discover new places, and uncover secrets at their own pace.

The game’s domain is registered through Natro, and it is hosted with Hosting Dünyam. Although our servers are located in Türkiye, the game is built with a global audience in mind. With support for multiple languages, it is steadily growing into a title that players around the world can enjoy.

Our Audience

The project is aimed primarily at children aged 7 to 12. We chose this age range for an important reason: the number of astronomers is declining. By sparking curiosity about the sky, the stars, and the universe at an early age, we hope to inspire the next generation of stargazers, scientists, and explorers, and to show them that science can be as exciting as any adventure.
